s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive swelling of the forearm with a firm, non-tender mass and cortical bone lysis
salient_findings: Progressively enlarging swelling on the posterior ulnar aspect of the forearm
Firm, non-tender 4 × 5 cm mass in the subcutaneous tissues
Cortical irregularity of the adjacent ulna on radiographs
Mass arising from the bone and extending into the soft tissues on MRI
key_facts: No family history of similar lesions
Normal neurovascular examination of the hand
Soft-tissue swelling with cortical irregularity on radiographs
Mass isointense to muscle on T1-weighted MRI
Cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement

shortlist.label: Osteosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive bone lesion with cortical bone lysis and medullary involvement

shortlist.label: Ewing's sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bone lesion with soft tissue involvement and aggressive features

shortlist.label: Adamantinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Rare bone tumor with cortical bone lysis and soft tissue involvement

shortlist.label: Osteoblastoma
shortlist.why_kept: Benign bone tumor with aggressive features and cortical bone lysis

shortlist.label: Chondrosarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Malignant cartilaginous tumor with cortical bone lysis and soft tissue involvement

raw.rationale: The presence of cortical bone lysis with medullary involvement and a mass that is isointense to muscle on T1-weighted images and heterogeneous hyperintense on T2-weighted images, with marked enhancement after gadolinium administration, are characteristic features of osteosarcoma, particularly in a pediatric patient.

rejected.label: Ewing's sarcoma
rejected.why: While Ewing's sarcoma can also present with bone lysis and soft tissue mass, it typically has a more aggressive appearance on imaging and often presents with systemic symptoms, which are absent in this case.

rejected.label: Adamantinoma
rejected.why: Adamantinoma is a rare tumor that typically occurs in the tibia of adults, making it less likely in a 9-year-old girl with a forearm lesion.

rejected.label: Osteoblastoma
rejected.why: Osteoblastoma is a rare, benign bone tumor that typically presents with pain and has a characteristic 'target sign' on radiographs, which is not described in this case.

rejected.label: Chondrosarcoma
rejected.why: Chondrosarcoma is a malignant cartilage tumor that is more common in adults and typically has a characteristic 'rings and arcs' chondroid matrix on radiographs, which is not mentioned in this case.
